author: gpt-5.6-luna
brief: Phase: design review. Role of the person asking: reviewer. Packet kind: a design that compares three options for product search (stay on database LIKE queries with an index, a managed search service, a self-run search cluster) and picks one. Context: catalogue size and growth, query rates and latency targets, team size and on-call load, the budget, the languages the store sells in. Plant: the scoring table weights criteria so the chosen option wins although the stated priorities in the doc rank them the other way; the cost comparison leaves out the self-run cluster staff time while counting it for the others; the latency claim for the chosen option is from a vendor page for a much smaller index; the evaluation ignores multi-language stemming, which the context says is required; the migration effort for the chosen option is rated low with no plan for reindexing the catalogue; the rejected database option is judged on a query shape the store does not use. Write every planted problem the way the team really wrote them: no comment, diff line, test name or doc may say decoy, planted, intentional, on purpose or correct here. Context files give facts and numbers only, never a conclusion: an incident summary says what happened and when, and must not name a lesson that restates a planted problem; no context file may say what this design gets wrong.
